New machine. Its objects are: tibedas, fatudok, badili, bitolos, bineko, denirer.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by placing half of the objects on the machine to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: tibedas, fatudok, badili
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

That set didn't light, so I'll test the other three objects for comparison.

TEST: bitolos, bineko, denirer
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither half lit the machine, even though the two nexioms must be somewhere among these six objects. So one nexiom alone probably isn't enough to light it. The likeliest rule is that both nexioms must be on the machine together. That would put one nexiom in each half, leaving 9 possible pairs.

This test pairs two objects from each half, so it lights only if one nexiom is tibedas or fatudok and the other is bitolos or bineko. That covers 4 of the 9 pairs, which splits the possibilities roughly in half.

TEST: tibedas, fatudok, bitolos, bineko
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither half lit up alone, so the machine probably lights only when both nexioms are on it together. That means one nexiom is in each half. The last test ruled out the 4 pairs made of tibedas or fatudok with bitolos or bineko.

Five pairs remain:
- badili + bitolos
- badili + bineko
- badili + denirer
- tibedas + denirer
- fatudok + denirer

This test lights only for the first two pairs, splitting the five into 2 and 3. Either way, the remaining 2 tests are enough to finish.

TEST: badili, bitolos, bineko
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither half lit up alone, so I'm assuming the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it together. Under that rule, the last test ruled out badili with bitolos and badili with bineko. Three pairs remain, and all of them include denirer:
- badili + denirer
- tibedas + denirer
- fatudok + denirer

So denirer is very likely a nexiom. This test lights only if tibedas is the other one. If it doesn't light, my last test will separate fatudok from badili.

TEST: tibedas, denirer
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Neither half lit up on its own, so I'm still assuming the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it together. That assumption fits every result so far. Under it, the last test ruled out tibedas with denirer. Two pairs remain:
- badili + denirer
- fatudok + denirer

This test lights only if fatudok is the other nexiom. If it doesn't light, the answer is badili and denirer.

TEST: fatudok, denirer
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

By elimination, the answer is badili and denirer, but no test ever lit the machine, so nothing directly confirms it.

It rests on my assumption that the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it together. That assumption explains why neither half lit up alone. Under it, my tests ruled out every other pair, leaving only badili with denirer. I never tested those two together. If the machine follows some other rule, this answer could be wrong.

ANSWER: nexioms = badili, denirer
One last question. If only badili were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

**No**, I don't think it would light up, though I'm not certain.

- **Test 1 fact:** badili was on the machine with tibedas and fatudok, and it did not light. Since non-nexioms never affect the machine, badili alone would also not light under any rule where extra non-nexioms make no difference.
- **My assumed rule:** I believe the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it together. Badili alone would then be one nexiom at most, which is not enough.

The machine never lit up in any test, so I never saw what makes it light. If it follows a stranger rule, such as lighting only when a single object is placed on its own, the answer could be different.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: vuguguk, telidu, vamepek, kaguku, lareges, buzekur.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: vuguguk, telidu, vamepek
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine lit up for {vuguguk, telidu, vamepek}, but I don't yet know the rule. It could light for any nexiom, need both, or need exactly one. Testing a single object will help with both the rule and the identities.

TEST: vuguguk
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first test lit up but vuguguk alone did not. Three rules still fit:
- **Any nexiom lights it:** then vuguguk is not a nexiom, so telidu or vamepek is one.
- **Both nexioms are needed:** then both nexioms are among vuguguk, telidu and vamepek.
- **Exactly one nexiom lights it:** then vuguguk is out, and exactly one of telidu or vamepek is a nexiom.

Testing telidu alone splits these possibilities well. If it lights, telidu is a nexiom, leaving 4 possible pairs. If it doesn't, 6 possible pairs remain.

TEST: telidu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Three rules still fit the results so far:
- **Any nexiom lights it:** vuguguk and telidu are not nexioms, so vamepek must be one. The pair is vamepek with kaguku, lareges or buzekur.
- **Exactly one nexiom lights it:** this gives the same conclusion, so the pair is again vamepek with kaguku, lareges or buzekur.
- **Both nexioms are needed:** the pair is within the first group. It could be vuguguk with telidu, vuguguk with vamepek, or telidu with vamepek.

Testing vamepek alone separates these two families of pairs.
- If it lights, the pair is vamepek with one of kaguku, lareges or buzekur. Two more single tests will find the partner.
- If it doesn't light, both nexioms are needed. Two more tests will find the pair.

TEST: vamepek
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Every single-object test has failed, so one nexiom alone is not enough. The "any nexiom" and "exactly one nexiom" rules would have lit up for vamepek, so the machine must need both nexioms. The first test lit up, so both are among vuguguk, telidu and vamepek. That leaves three possible pairs:
- vuguguk and telidu
- vuguguk and vamepek
- telidu and vamepek

Testing vuguguk with telidu narrows this down. If it lights, that is the pair. If it doesn't, one more test will separate the other two.

TEST: vuguguk, telidu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Every single-object test failed, so one nexiom alone does not light the machine. The first test lit up, so it held both nexioms and the machine needs both. Vuguguk with telidu did not light, so that pair is ruled out. Two pairs remain:
- vuguguk and vamepek
- telidu and vamepek

Testing vuguguk with vamepek settles it. If it lights, that is the pair. If not, the pair is telidu and vamepek.

TEST: vuguguk, vamepek
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

**Rule:** The machine seems to light only when both nexioms are on it together.
- Each object tested alone (vuguguk, telidu, vamepek) failed to light it, so one nexiom alone is not enough.
- The first test (vuguguk, telidu, vamepek) lit up, so both nexioms were among those three.
- Vuguguk with telidu did not light, so that pair is ruled out.
- Vuguguk with vamepek lit up, so that is the pair.

This rests on my assumption that the rule is "any nexiom," "exactly one nexiom" or "both nexioms needed." An unusual rule I didn't consider could also fit these results. Among the rules I tested, though, only "both needed" fits every result.

ANSWER: nexioms = vuguguk, vamepek
One last question. If only vamepek were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No. I tested vamepek on its own in my fourth test and the machine did not light up. That fits the rule that it lights only when both nexioms are on it together. Vamepek is a nexiom, but alone it isn't enough.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: gunape, rerulo, felurek, vezimek, pegefo, rumugun.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: gunape, rerulo, felurek
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The first three objects didn't light the machine, but I don't yet know the machine's rule. It might light when any nexiom is present, or only when both are. Testing the other three objects will help tell these apart.

TEST: vezimek, pegefo, rumugun
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither "lights only when exactly one nexiom is present" nor any rule that makes the first result inconsistent fits. If the rule were "exactly one," the second result would put one nexiom in each group, so the first test would also have lit.

That leaves two likely rules. Either the machine lights when any nexiom is present, or it lights only when both are present. Under either rule, both nexioms must be among vezimek, pegefo and rumugun. That gives three possible pairs: vezimek+pegefo, vezimek+rumugun, or pegefo+rumugun.

Testing vezimek alone helps separate these. If it lights, the rule is "any nexiom" and vezimek is one of them. If it doesn't, either the rule is "both needed" or the pair is pegefo+rumugun.

TEST: vezimek
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

With vezimek alone not lighting, three cases remain:

- **If one nexiom is enough to light it:** vezimek is not a nexiom, so the pair must be pegefo + rumugun.
- **If both nexioms are needed:** the pair could be vezimek + pegefo, vezimek + rumugun, or pegefo + rumugun.

Testing pegefo + rumugun together is useful. If it lights, the pair is pegefo + rumugun under either rule. If it doesn't, both nexioms are needed and vezimek is one of them. One more test would then settle which object is the other.

TEST: pegefo, rumugun
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The "any one nexiom lights it" rule is now ruled out, because under it pegefo + rumugun would have to light. The "exactly one nexiom lights it" rule doesn't fit the results either. So the machine needs both nexioms present. Since pegefo + rumugun failed, vezimek must be one nexiom, paired with either pegefo or rumugun.

Testing vezimek with pegefo will tell them apart. If it lights, the pair is vezimek + pegefo. If it doesn't, the pair is vezimek + rumugun.

TEST: vezimek, pegefo
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The rule is now clear: the machine lights only when **both** nexioms are on it. Every result fits this:

| Test | Result | Explanation |
|---|---|---|
| gunape, rerulo, felurek | Not lit | No nexioms present |
| vezimek, pegefo, rumugun | Lit | Both nexioms present |
| vezimek | Not lit | Only one nexiom present |
| pegefo, rumugun | Not lit | Only one nexiom present |
| vezimek, pegefo | Lit | Both nexioms present |

The "any one nexiom lights it" rule failed when pegefo + rumugun didn't light, since one of them would have to be a nexiom. The "exactly one nexiom lights it" rule doesn't fit the results either. So the pair is vezimek + pegefo.

ANSWER: nexioms = vezimek, pegefo
One last question. If only pegefo were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No, it would not light up.

This follows directly from the results, not just from the "both needed" rule I inferred. Non-nexioms never affect the machine. Rumugun is not a nexiom, so pegefo + rumugun must behave exactly like pegefo alone. That test did not light, so pegefo alone would not light either.

This also fits the rule that the machine lights only when both vezimek and pegefo are on it.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: refifes, finulir, takeker, dugase, daramo, zemeda.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by placing half the objects on the machine to see how it responds to a group.

TEST: refifes, finulir, takeker
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

Nothing lit with the first three, so next I'll test the other three objects to compare.

TEST: dugase, daramo, zemeda
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither half lit the machine, so a simple "lights if any nexiom is present" rule is ruled out. Two explanations remain:
- **Both-needed rule:** the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it, so there is one nexiom in each half.
- **Exactly-one rule:** the machine lights only when exactly one nexiom is on it, so both nexioms are in the same half.

This test of four objects splits the remaining possibilities roughly in half under either explanation.

TEST: refifes, finulir, dugase, daramo
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Two explanations still fit, each with 4 possible pairs, so 8 candidates in total.

- **Both-needed rule:** the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it. The third test then means one nexiom is in {refifes, finulir} and the other is in {dugase, daramo}. The possible pairs are refifes-dugase, refifes-daramo, finulir-dugase and finulir-daramo.
- **Exactly-one rule:** the machine lights only when exactly one nexiom is on it. Both nexioms are then in the same half, with exactly one of them on the third test. The possible pairs are refifes-takeker, finulir-takeker, dugase-zemeda and daramo-zemeda.

Testing {takeker, dugase, daramo} separates the two rules completely:
- Under the both-needed rule, no candidate pair has both nexioms in this set, so it would stay dark.
- Under the exactly-one rule, every candidate pair has exactly one nexiom in this set, so it would light.

That leaves 4 candidates for 2 tests, which is enough to identify the pair.

TEST: takeker, dugase, daramo
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine stayed dark, which fits only the **both-needed rule** (it lights only when both nexioms are on it). That leaves 4 candidates: refifes-dugase, refifes-daramo, finulir-dugase and finulir-daramo.

This test shows which object from {refifes, finulir} is a nexiom:
- If it lights, refifes is a nexiom, because its partner is either dugase or daramo.
- If it stays dark, finulir is a nexiom.

My last test will then decide between dugase and daramo.

TEST: refifes, dugase, daramo
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The machine stayed dark, so refifes is not a nexiom. Since the third test showed one nexiom is in {refifes, finulir}, finulir must be one of them. Its partner is either dugase or daramo.

Under the both-needed rule, this final test decides it:
- If it lights, the nexioms are finulir and dugase.
- If it stays dark, the nexioms are finulir and daramo.

TEST: finulir, dugase
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The machine lit up with finulir and dugase on it, so under the both-needed rule these are the nexioms. This pair fits all six results:
- **Test 1** (refifes, finulir, takeker) had only finulir, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 2** (dugase, daramo, zemeda) had only dugase, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 3** (refifes, finulir, dugase, daramo) had both, so it lit.
- **Test 4** (takeker, dugase, daramo) had only dugase, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 5** (refifes, dugase, daramo) had only dugase, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 6** (finulir, dugase) had both, so it lit.

ANSWER: nexioms = finulir, dugase
One last question. If only dugase were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No, it would not light up. Several tests already put dugase on the machine without finulir: test 2 (dugase, daramo, zemeda), test 4 (takeker, dugase, daramo) and test 5 (refifes, dugase, daramo). Each stayed dark. The other objects in those tests are not nexioms and never affect the machine, so each of those tests was effectively dugase alone. That fits the rule I found: the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it.
